solution:

question_latex: A particle moves so that its position vector is given by $\vec{r}=cos~\omega t\hat{x}+sin~\omega t\hat{y}$. Where $\omega$ is a constant. Which of the following is true?
options: Velocity is perpendicular to $\vec{r}$ and acceleration is directed towards the origin.
Velocity is perpendicular to $\vec{r}$ and acceleration is directed away from the origin.
Velocity and acceleration both are perpendicular to $\vec{r}$
Velocity and acceleration both are parallel to $\vec{r}$
solution:
$\vec{r} = \cos(\omega t)\hat{i} + \sin(\omega t)\hat{j}$. 
$\vec{v} = \frac{d\vec{r}}{dt} = -\omega\sin(\omega t)\hat{i} + \omega\cos(\omega t)\hat{j}$. 
$\vec{a} = \frac{d\vec{v}}{dt} = -\omega^2\cos(\omega t)\hat{i} - \omega^2\sin(\omega t)\hat{j} = -\omega^2 \vec{r}$. 
Dot product $\vec{r} \cdot \vec{v} = -\omega \sin\cos + \omega \sin\cos = 0$. So $\vec{v} \perp \vec{r}$. 
$\vec{a} = -\omega^2 \vec{r}$, so acceleration is directed towards the origin (opposite to $\vec{r}$).

question_latex: An electric dipole is placed in a non-uniform electric field whose field lines diverge as one moves from left to right (i.e., the field strength is greater on the left and decreases towards the right). options: Towards the left as its potential energy will increase.
Towards the right as its potential energy will decrease.
Towards the left as its potential energy will decrease.
Towards the right as its potential energy will increase.
solution: Potential energy $U = -\vec{P} \cdot \vec{E}$. Also, the net force is dominated by the field at +q (stronger field on left) pushing right vs force on -q pulling left (weaker field on right). Net force is towards the right.

question_latex: A car starts from rest and accelerates at $5~m/s^{2}$ At $t=4$ s, a ball is dropped out of a window by a person sitting in the car. What is the velocity and acceleration of the ball at $t=6$ s?

Velocity of car at t=4s: $v_x = u + at = 0 + 5(4) = 20$ m/s.

question_latex: Ten E.coli cells with 15N - dsDNA are incubated in medium containing 14N nucleotide. After 60 minutes, how many E.coli cells will have DNA totally free from 15N?

E. coli divides every 20 mins. 60 mins = 3 generations. 
Start: 10 cells ($^{15}N^{15}N$). 
Gen 1 (20 min): 20 cells (all hybrid $^{15}N^{14}N$). 
Gen 2 (40 min): 40 cells (20 hybrid, 20 pure $^{14}N$). 
Gen 3 (60 min): 80 cells.

The 20 pure $^{14}N$ strands from Gen 2 split: 20 $^{14}N$ + 20 new $^{14}N$ -> 40 pure.

Hybrid ($^{15}N^{14}N$) = 20. 
Free from $^{15}N$ (Pure $^{14}N$) = $80 - 20 = 60$.

The ratio of the moment of inertia of the smaller scooped-out sphere about a diameter of itself to the moment of inertia of the remaining body (the larger sphere minus the cavity) about the same axis (passing through the centre of the small sphere) is:
solution: Sol: $I_{small} = 7/40 MR^2$. Ratio to remaining is 7/57.

question_latex: A container has two chambers of volumes $V_1 = 2$ litres and $V_2 = 3$ litres separated by a partition. The chambers contain $n_1 = 5$ and $n_2 = 4$ moles of ideal gas at pressures $P_1 = 1$ atm and $P_2 = 2$ atm. When partition is removed, equilibrium pressure is:
solution: Total internal energy is conserved (or simply partial pressures add if T is constant, but better $P_{mix} = (P_1 V_1 + P_2 V_2) / (V_1 + V_2)$). $P = (1 \times 2 + 2 \times 3) / (2 + 3) = (2 + 6)/5 = 8/5 = 1.6$ atm.
